scenarios.title: Valid App with Provider and Consumer References
scenarios.description: An App definition includes a ServiceProviderReference and a ServiceConsumerReference that both reference services defined elsewhere in the system configuration.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation succeeds; both ServiceProviderReference and ServiceConsumerReference resolve to existing services and the App is bound to the specified ECU controller without errors.

scenarios.title: Dangling ServiceConsumerReference
scenarios.description: The ServiceConsumerReference within an App points to a service identifier that is not defined in any ServiceProviderReference in the system.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation fails with error code DanglingServiceConsumerReference indicating the referenced service cannot be resolved.
scenarios.injected_fault: missing or dangling reference (ServiceConsumerReference pointing to a non-existent service)

scenarios.title: Valid AppBindings Mapping
scenarios.description: An AppBindings file maps a uniquely identified App to a specific ECU controller, and the App identifier does not appear elsewhere.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation succeeds; AppBindings correctly links the App to the ECU controller and the App identifier is confirmed unique system‑wide.

scenarios.title: Duplicate App Identifier
scenarios.description: Two separate App definition files use the same App identifier, violating the system‑wide uniqueness constraint.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation fails with error code DuplicateAppIdentifier indicating the App identifier is used more than once.
scenarios.injected_fault: duplicate identifier (App identifier)

scenarios.title: Valid ServiceProviderReference
scenarios.description: A ServiceProviderReference in an App specifies a transport service (e.g., SOME/IP) that exists in the system's service catalog.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation succeeds; ServiceProviderReference resolves to an existing service definition.

scenarios.title: Out‑of‑Range Port Number
scenarios.description: A ServiceProviderReference defines a port number value of 70000, which exceeds the maximum allowed value of 65535.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation fails with error code PortNumberOutOfRange indicating the port number must be within 0‑65535.
scenarios.injected_fault: out-of-range value at or beyond a boundary (port number)

scenarios.title: Valid AppBindings on Multiple Controllers
scenarios.description: An App is referenced by AppBindings entries on three different ECU controllers, each entry using the same unique App identifier.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation succeeds; the App is deployed to all specified controllers and the App identifier remains unique system‑wide.

scenarios.title: Missing AppBindings
scenarios.description: An App definition is present but no AppBindings file references it, leaving the App without any deployment target.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation fails with error code MissingAppBindings indicating the App has no binding to any ECU controller.
scenarios.injected_fault: missing or dangling reference (App without AppBindings)

scenarios.title: Valid ServiceConsumerReference to Existing Service
scenarios.description: A ServiceConsumerReference in an App points to a service identifier that is defined by an existing ServiceProviderReference.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation succeeds; ServiceConsumerReference resolves to the existing service without errors.

scenarios.title: CAN Bus Configuration Validation
scenarios.description: A CAN bus is defined with a unique name and includes valid participating nodes and frames in its bus‑level parameters.
scenarios.expected_result: The CAN bus configuration is accepted, the bus name is extracted from the "name" field, and no validation errors are reported.

scenarios.title: Duplicate CAN Bus Name
scenarios.description: A second CAN bus definition uses a name that already exists in the system.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation fails with error code DUPLICATE_BUS_NAME; the duplicate bus is not added to the model.
scenarios.injected_fault: duplicate bus name

scenarios.title: LIN Bus Master Node Validation
scenarios.description: A LIN bus configuration contains exactly one master node and several slave nodes, and all schedule tables reference frames that are defined in the "frames" section.
scenarios.expected_result: The LIN bus configuration is accepted, the single master node is identified, and schedule tables resolve all frame references.

scenarios.title: Missing Frame Reference in LIN Schedule Table
scenarios.description: A LIN schedule table entry references a frame name that is not present in the bus's "frames" list.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation fails with error code MISSING_FRAME_REFERENCE indicating the undefined frame name; the LIN bus definition is rejected.
scenarios.injected_fault: missing frame reference

scenarios.title: Valid CAN Bus Frame with Correct PDU Reference
scenarios.description: A CAN bus frame is defined with a valid "pdu_ref" that points to an existing PDU and its payload size complies with classic CAN limits (0‑8 bytes).
scenarios.expected_result: The frame is accepted, the PDU reference resolves, and the frame is considered correctly transmitted on the bus.

scenarios.title: LIN Schedule Table Timing Conflict
scenarios.description: A LIN schedule table entry specifies a start_time that exceeds the bus cycle length, creating a timing conflict.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation fails with error code SCHEDULE_TIMING_CONFLICT; the LIN bus definition is not created.
scenarios.injected_fault: schedule timing out of range

scenarios.title: Valid LIN Slave Node PID Configuration
scenarios.description: A LIN slave node is configured with a unique PID within the allowed range (0‑15) and correctly responds to the master’s PID requests.
scenarios.expected_result: The slave node passes validation, its PID is accepted, and the node is linked to the LIN bus as a functional slave.

scenarios.title: Duplicate LIN Slave Node PID
scenarios.description: Two LIN slave nodes on the same bus are configured with the same PID value.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation fails with error code DUPLICATE_SLAVE_PID; the second slave node is rejected.
scenarios.injected_fault: duplicate LIN slave PID

scenarios.title: CAN Bus Configuration File Location and Parameter Validation
scenarios.description: A CAN bus YAML file is placed in the required ``communication/channels/can/`` directory and contains all mandatory bus‑level fields (e.g., name, nodes, frames).
scenarios.expected_result: The file is successfully parsed, the bus definition is loaded, and no file‑location or missing‑parameter errors are reported.

scenarios.title: Valid FLYNCChannelConfig with Correct Bus and PDU Definitions
scenarios.description: A FLYNCChannelConfig is created with valid bus definitions (e.g., CAN bus ID 0, bitrate 500 kbps) and valid PDU definitions stored under communication/channels/, and all fields are correctly populated.
scenarios.expected_result: Validator returns success; no errors are reported and the FLYNCChannelConfig instance is created with the provided bus and PDU definitions.

scenarios.title: Invalid TCPOption with Duplicate TCP Profile Name
scenarios.description: A TCPOption references a TCP profile named "default" that is defined more than once in tcp_profiles.flync.yaml, violating the uniqueness requirement for TCP profile identifiers.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation fails with error DUPLICATE_PROFILE_NAME indicating that the TCP profile name "default" is defined multiple times.
scenarios.injected_fault: duplicate profile name

scenarios.title: Valid UDPOption with Correct Port Number
scenarios.description: A UDPOption is created with a valid port number 5000 (within the 0‑65535 range and not reserved for well‑known services), and all required fields are populated.
scenarios.expected_result: Validator returns success; the UDPOption instance is created with port 5000 and no errors are reported.

scenarios.title: Invalid FLYNCChannelConfig with CAN Bus Bitrate Exceeding Maximum
scenarios.description: A FLYNCChannelConfig defines a CAN bus bitrate of 5 Mbit/s, which exceeds the allowed maximum of 1 Mbit/s for classic CAN buses.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation fails with error BUS_BITRATE_OUT_OF_RANGE indicating that the specified bitrate (5 Mbit/s) is above the permitted maximum.
scenarios.injected_fault: out-of-range value at or beyond a boundary

scenarios.title: Valid TCPOption with Correct TCP Profile
scenarios.description: A TCPOption is created with a valid TCP profile "high_performance" imported from tcp_profiles.flync.yaml, and all fields are correctly populated.
scenarios.expected_result: Validator returns success; the TCPOption instance is created using the "high_performance" profile without errors.

scenarios.title: Invalid UDPOption with Dangling Layer4Endpoint Reference
scenarios.description: A UDPOption references a Layer4Endpoint identifier "ECU1_UdpSock" that is not defined in any ECU's socket configuration, creating a dangling reference.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation fails with error DANGLING_REFERENCE indicating that Layer4Endpoint "ECU1_UdpSock" does not exist.
scenarios.injected_fault: missing or dangling reference

scenarios.title: Invalid TCPOption with Unreachable VLAN Path
scenarios.description: A TCPOption is assigned to VLAN ID 20, but the system configuration lacks a VLAN entry for ID 20 on the switch connecting the transmitter and receiver, making the path unreachable.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation fails with error VLAN_PATH_UNREACHABLE indicating that VLAN ID 20 is not configured on the required switch.
scenarios.injected_fault: unreachable multicast/VLAN path

scenarios.title: Valid UDPOption with Correct IPv6 Address
scenarios.description: A UDPOption is created with a valid IPv6 address "2001:db8::1", and all required fields are correctly populated.
scenarios.expected_result: Validator returns success; the UDPOption instance is created with IPv6 address 2001:db8::1 and no errors are reported.

scenarios.title: Invalid MultiplexedPDU with Undefined Selector Value
scenarios.description: A MultiplexedPDU is configured with a selector signal value of 99, but the selector mapping does not define a PDU for this value, violating the rule that every selector value must map to a valid PDU.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation fails with error UNDEFINED_MUX_SELECTOR indicating that selector value 99 has no associated PDU.
scenarios.injected_fault: undefined selector value

scenarios.title: Valid ECU configuration with one mandatory controller and one port
scenarios.description: ECU configuration includes a single ECUPort entry and a Controller directory containing at least one Controller, satisfying the mandatory requirements of the ECU and ECU Ports Config sections.
scenarios.expected_result: Validator returns success; no errors are reported for ECU, ECUPort, or Controller definitions.

scenarios.title: Duplicate ECUPort identifier causes validation error
scenarios.description: ECU configuration defines two ECUPort objects with the same identifier value 'portA', violating the uniqueness constraint for port identifiers.
scenarios.expected_result: Validator fails with error indicating duplicate ECUPort identifier 'portA'.
scenarios.injected_fault: duplicate identifier

scenarios.title: Valid Virtual Switch with a correctly defined VirtualSwitchPort
scenarios.description: VirtualSwitch configuration includes a VirtualSwitchPort named 'vs_port1' with matching MAC address and VLAN ID, adhering to the Virtual Switch schema.
scenarios.expected_result: Validator returns success; VirtualSwitch and VirtualSwitchPort are accepted.

scenarios.title: Switch configuration with VLAN ID out of allowed range
scenarios.description: Switch YAML defines a VLAN entry with ID 5000, which exceeds the IEEE 802.1Q valid range (1‑4094).
scenarios.expected_result: Validator fails, reporting 'VLAN ID 5000 out of range (must be 1‑4094)' for the Switch configuration.
scenarios.injected_fault: out-of-range value

scenarios.title: Socket with valid IPv4 address endpoint
scenarios.description: Socket definition uses IPv4AddressEndpoint with address '192.168.10.5' and port 13400, both within allowed ranges.
scenarios.expected_result: Validator returns success; Socket and IPv4AddressEndpoint pass validation.

scenarios.title: ECU missing mandatory controllers directory
scenarios.description: ECU configuration omits the required 'controllers/' directory, leaving the ECU without any defined Controller objects.
scenarios.expected_result: Validator fails, reporting 'Missing mandatory controllers directory for ECU' error.
scenarios.injected_fault: missing or dangling reference

scenarios.title: Ethernet Interface includes required MII configuration for external PHY
scenarios.description: EthernetInterface entry references an external PHY and provides a complete mii_config block with valid phy_address and speed settings.
scenarios.expected_result: Validator returns success; EthernetInterface and its MII configuration are accepted.

scenarios.title: CAN Interface with Classic CAN payload length exceeding 8 bytes
scenarios.description: CANInterface definition sets DLC to 12 for a Classic CAN frame, violating the maximum payload size of 8 bytes.
scenarios.expected_result: Validator fails, reporting 'Classic CAN DLC 12 exceeds maximum of 8 bytes' error.
scenarios.injected_fault: size mismatch

scenarios.title: Valid LIN Master Interface configuration
scenarios.description: LINMasterInterface defines a master with PID 0x30, supported slave count 4, and a schedule table conforming to LIN specifications.
scenarios.expected_result: Validator returns success; LINMasterInterface passes validation.

scenarios.title: Virtual Switch references multicast VLAN without corresponding VLAN entry
scenarios.description: VirtualSwitch configuration includes a multicast group on VLAN 100, but the Switch configuration does not contain VLAN 100, making the path unreachable.
scenarios.expected_result: Validator fails, reporting 'Multicast group VLAN 100 not defined in any Switch configuration' error.
scenarios.injected_fault: unreachable multicast/VLAN path

scenarios.title: SystemMetadata with valid semver version
scenarios.description: Create a SystemMetadata instance with system_id='SYS001' and version='2.1.4' (Semantic Versioning 2.0.0).
scenarios.expected_result: Validation succeeds; no errors are reported.

scenarios.title: ECUMetadata duplicate identifier detection
scenarios.description: Create two ECUMetadata instances both with identifier='ECU_A'. The second instance should trigger duplicate identifier validation.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation fails with DuplicateIdentifierError indicating identifier 'ECU_A' is already used.
scenarios.injected_fault: duplicate identifier

scenarios.title: BaseVersion accepts valid semver string
scenarios.description: Instantiate BaseVersion with version='3.0.0'.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation succeeds; version string is parsed as a valid Semantic Version.

scenarios.title: HardwareBaseMetadata rejects malformed version string
scenarios.description: Create a HardwareBaseMetadata with version='v1' which does not conform to semver or PEP 440.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation fails with VersionParseError indicating the version 'v1' is invalid.
scenarios.injected_fault: malformed version string

scenarios.title: EmbeddedMetadata references existing ECUMetadata
scenarios.description: Create an ECUMetadata with identifier='ECU_B' and then an EmbeddedMetadata with parent_ecu_id='ECU_B'.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation succeeds; parent_ecu_id resolves to an existing ECUMetadata.

scenarios.title: SystemMetadata accepts PEP 440 version string
scenarios.description: Create a SystemMetadata with system_id='SYS002' and version='1.0rc1' (PEP 440 compliant).
scenarios.expected_result: Validation succeeds; version string is recognized as a valid PEP 440 version.

scenarios.title: ECUMetadata missing required system_id field
scenarios.description: Instantiate ECUMetadata without providing the mandatory 'system_id' attribute.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation fails with MissingFieldError indicating that 'system_id' is required.
scenarios.injected_fault: missing mandatory field

scenarios.title: BaseMetadata with valid semver version
scenarios.description: Create a BaseMetadata instance with version='0.0.1'.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation succeeds; version string parses as a valid Semantic Version.

scenarios.title: StateManagementGroup with valid nm_pdu and timing_profile resolves membership
scenarios.description: A StateManagementGroup named VEHICLE is configured with nm_pdu set to PDU_NmMessage and timing_profile set to "standard". Entity‑side state_memberships declare participation in this group, so the validator must derive the correct member set.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation succeeds; the StateManagementGroup is accepted and its derived membership list matches the StateMembershipRef entries declared on the entities.

scenarios.title: Duplicate StateManagementGroup names cause validation error
scenarios.description: Two StateManagementGroup entries are defined with the identical name "VEHICLE" in groups.flync.yaml.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation fails with error "DuplicateGroupNameError" indicating that the group name "VEHICLE" is used more than once.
scenarios.injected_fault: duplicate identifier (Group name)

scenarios.title: GroupTiming with valid cycle_time_ms, announcement, and sleep passes validation
scenarios.description: A GroupTiming profile named "standard" specifies cycle_time_ms = 500, announcement.duration_ms = 1000, announcement.burst_count = 5, announcement.burst_cycle_time_ms = 20, sleep.timeout_ms = 2000, and sleep.wait_before_sleep_ms = 1500.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation succeeds; all timing values are within allowed ranges and the GroupTiming object is accepted.

scenarios.title: GroupTiming with negative cycle_time_ms fails validation
scenarios.description: A GroupTiming profile sets cycle_time_ms = -10, which is below the minimum allowed value of 0.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation fails with error "InvalidCycleTimeError" because cycle_time_ms is negative.
scenarios.injected_fault: out-of-range value at or beyond a boundary (cycle_time_ms)

scenarios.title: StateMembershipRef with participant role and valid relevance bits passes
scenarios.description: A StateMembershipRef declares group = "VEHICLE", role = "participant", and relevance_bits = ["AutonomousDriving", "OnlineCommunication"].
scenarios.expected_result: Validation succeeds; the StateMembershipRef is accepted and the relevance bits are resolved correctly.

scenarios.title: SleepTiming with positive timeout_ms and wait_before_sleep_ms passes
scenarios.description: A SleepTiming entry specifies timeout_ms = 2000 and wait_before_sleep_ms = 1500.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation succeeds; both timeout_ms and wait_before_sleep_ms are within the allowed non‑negative range.

scenarios.title: SleepTiming with negative timeout_ms fails validation
scenarios.description: A SleepTiming entry sets timeout_ms = -5, which is below the minimum allowed value of 0.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation fails with error "InvalidTimeoutError" because timeout_ms is negative.
scenarios.injected_fault: out-of-range value at or beyond a boundary (timeout_ms)

scenarios.title: AnnouncementPhaseTiming with valid duration, burst_count, and burst_cycle_time_ms passes
scenarios.description: An AnnouncementPhaseTiming defines duration_ms = 1000, burst_count = 5, and burst_cycle_time_ms = 20.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation succeeds; all announcement timing fields are within their permitted ranges.

scenarios.title: AnnouncementPhaseTiming with negative burst_count fails validation
scenarios.description: An AnnouncementPhaseTiming sets burst_count = -1, which is below the allowed minimum of 0.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation fails with error "InvalidBurstCountError" because burst_count cannot be negative.
scenarios.injected_fault: out-of-range value at or beyond a boundary (burst_count)

scenarios.title: MACsecConfig with IntegrityWithConfidentiality
scenarios.description: Create a MACsecConfig object that references an IntegrityWithConfidentiality instance, thereby enabling both integrity protection and confidentiality for Ethernet frames.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation succeeds; the MACsecConfig instance is created and its confidentiality flag is set to true.

scenarios.title: FirewallRule with destination port 70000 (out of range)
scenarios.description: Create a FirewallRule where destination_port = 70000 (greater than the maximum allowed 65535) while all other fields (source_ip, destination_ip, source_port, protocol) contain valid values.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation fails with error message: "Destination port 70000 is outside the valid range 0‑65535."
scenarios.injected_fault: out-of-range value at or beyond a boundary (max payload, max ID, max timeout)

scenarios.title: MACsecConfig with IntegrityWithoutConfidentiality
scenarios.description: Create a MACsecConfig object that references an IntegrityWithoutConfidentiality instance, providing integrity protection but no payload encryption.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation succeeds; the MACsecConfig instance is created and its confidentiality flag is set to false.

scenarios.title: Duplicate FirewallRule with identical match criteria
scenarios.description: Create two FirewallRule objects that have exactly the same source_ip, destination_ip, source_port, destination_port, and protocol values.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation fails with error message: "Duplicate firewall rule detected – identical match criteria already exist."
scenarios.injected_fault: duplicate identifier (IP, MAC, Service ID, Frame ID)

scenarios.title: Firewall containing three distinct FirewallRules
scenarios.description: Create a Firewall object that includes three FirewallRule entries, each with unique source/destination IP addresses and ports.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation succeeds; the Firewall is created containing the three distinct rules.

scenarios.title: MACsecConfig referencing a non‑existent Integrity mode
scenarios.description: Create a MACsecConfig whose integrity_mode field points to an IntegrityWithConfidentiality object that is not defined elsewhere in the model.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation fails with error message: "Integrity mode reference is dangling – referenced object does not exist."
scenarios.injected_fault: missing or dangling reference (forwarder pointing to a non-existent socket/ECU)

scenarios.title: FirewallRule with destination port 8080 (valid)
scenarios.description: Create a FirewallRule with destination_port = 8080, source_ip = "192.168.1.10", destination_ip = "192.168.1.20", source_port = 12345, and protocol = TCP.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation succeeds; the rule is accepted as a valid FirewallRule.

scenarios.title: Firewall with a single valid FirewallRule
scenarios.description: Create a Firewall that contains exactly one FirewallRule with valid fields (e.g., source_ip = "10.0.0.1", destination_ip = "10.0.0.2", source_port = 1000, destination_port = 2000, protocol = UDP).
scenarios.expected_result: Validation succeeds; the Firewall is created containing the single valid rule.

scenarios.title: Valid UINT8 Signal with Matching Bit Length
scenarios.description: Define a Signal with data_type UINT8, bit_length 8, and no value encoding. The bit length equals the natural bit width of UINT8.
scenarios.expected_result: Validator accepts the Signal; no errors are reported.

scenarios.title: Signal Bit Length Exceeds UINT16 Capacity
scenarios.description: Define a Signal with data_type UINT16 and bit_length 20. The bit length is larger than the 16‑bit natural width of UINT16.
scenarios.expected_result: Validator rejects the Signal with an error indicating that bit_length (20) exceeds the natural bit width of UINT16 (16).
scenarios.injected_fault: bit_length of 20 declared on a UINT16 signal (max 16 bits)

scenarios.title: Enumerated Signal Using Text Table Encoding
scenarios.description: Define a Signal with data_type UINT8, bit_length 8, and value_encoding of type text_table containing entries mapping 0→'Park', 1→'Reverse', 2→'Neutral', 3→'Drive'.
scenarios.expected_result: Validator accepts the Signal; the text_table entries are stored without overlap or missing fields.

scenarios.title: Duplicate Signal Name Within a Model
scenarios.description: Create two Signal objects in the same model both named 'VehicleSpeed'.
scenarios.expected_result: Validator reports a duplicate identifier error for Signal name 'VehicleSpeed'.
scenarios.injected_fault: duplicate identifier (Signal name)

scenarios.title: Signal with Bitfield Text Table Encoding
scenarios.description: Define a 16‑bit Signal with value_encoding type bitfield_text_table. It contains two BitfieldGroup entries: group 'Problem' mask 0x00FF with states 0→'NoProblem', 1→'Minor', 2→'Major'; and group 'Mode' mask 0xFF00 with states 0x0000→'Off', 0x0100→'On'.
scenarios.expected_result: Validator accepts the Signal; each BitfieldGroup mask is disjoint and each group's states are non‑overlapping, allowing correct decoding.

scenarios.title: Bitmask Flags Encoding with Overlapping Masks
scenarios.description: Define a Signal with value_encoding type bitmask_flags containing two flags: FlagA mask 0x0003 and FlagB mask 0x0002 (overlap on bit 1).
scenarios.expected_result: Validator rejects the Signal with an error indicating that flag masks are not disjoint (FlagA and FlagB overlap).
scenarios.injected_fault: invalid bitmask flag (mask not disjoint)

scenarios.title: Signal with Linear Scaling and Unit
scenarios.description: Define a Signal with data_type UINT8, bit_length 8, factor 0.5, offset -40.0, unit 'degC', lower_limit -40.0, upper_limit 215.0, and a value_encoding that maps 254→'Sensor_Error' and 255→'Signal_Not_Available'.
scenarios.expected_result: Validator accepts the Signal; linear conversion (raw*0.5‑40) is applied to raw values not covered by the text_table, and limits are respected.

scenarios.title: SignalInstance Placement Extends Beyond Signal Bit Length
scenarios.description: Define a Signal with bit_length 8. Create a SignalInstance with placement bit_offset 5 and length 8 (i.e., occupies bits 5‑12).
scenarios.expected_result: Validator rejects the SignalInstance with an error indicating placement exceeds the owning Signal's bit length (bits 5‑12 out of range for an 8‑bit signal).
scenarios.injected_fault: invalid instance placement (exceeds signal bit length)

scenarios.title: Signal Combining Text Table Encoding with Linear Conversion
scenarios.description: Define a Signal with data_type UINT16, bit_length 16, factor 0.1, offset 0, unit 'km/h', and value_encoding type text_table mapping 65535→'Signal_Not_Available'.
scenarios.expected_result: Validator accepts the Signal; raw value 65535 is interpreted as 'Signal_Not_Available', all other raw values are converted using the linear formula and fall within the expected physical range.

scenarios.title: Value Encoding Entry Missing Required Label Field
scenarios.description: Define a Signal with value_encoding type text_table containing an entry that specifies value: 1 but omits the required 'label' field.
scenarios.expected_result: Validator rejects the Signal with an error indicating that the value_encoding entry is missing the required field 'label'.
scenarios.injected_fault: missing or dangling reference (value encoding entry)

scenarios.title: Valid SOMEIPServiceInterface with unique Service ID and optional elements
scenarios.description: Create a SOMEIPServiceInterface instance named 'EngineControl' with Service Identifier 0x1234, and include at least one Field, one Event, and one Method. All identifiers are unique and references resolve.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation succeeds; the interface is accepted and can be referenced by providers and consumers.

scenarios.title: Duplicate Service Identifier in two SOMEIPServiceInterface objects
scenarios.description: Define two SOMEIPServiceInterface objects: first with Service Identifier 0x2000, second also with Service Identifier 0x2000. Both otherwise valid.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation fails with error "Service Identifier 0x2000 is already used by another SOMEIPServiceInterface" and the second interface is rejected.
scenarios.injected_fault: duplicate identifier (Service ID)

scenarios.title: Valid SOMEIPRequestResponseMethod with correct return type and parameters
scenarios.description: Create a SOMEIPRequestResponseMethod named 'GetEngineSpeed' returning uint16 and accepting a single input parameter of type uint8 named 'requestId'.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation succeeds; the method is added to the service interface without errors.

scenarios.title: Eventgroup referencing a non‑existent SOMEIPEvent
scenarios.description: Define a SOMEIPEventgroup 'EngineEvents' that lists an event identifier 'EngineOverheat' which is not defined in any SOMEIPEvent object.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation fails with error "Eventgroup EngineEvents references undefined event EngineOverheat".
scenarios.injected_fault: missing or dangling reference (Eventgroup pointing to a non-existent event)

scenarios.title: Valid SOMEIPField with getter and setter methods
scenarios.description: Create a SOMEIPField named 'VehicleSpeed' of datatype uint16, with associated getter method 'GetSpeed' and setter method 'SetSpeed', both correctly defined.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation succeeds; the field is accepted and its getter/setter are linked.

scenarios.title: SOMEIPServiceDeployment referencing missing Layer4Endpoint
scenarios.description: Instantiate a SOMEIPServiceDeployment for service ID 0x3000 and set its endpoint reference to a Layer4Endpoint named 'ECU1_EP' that does not exist in the model.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation fails with error "SOMEIPServiceDeployment for service 0x3000 references undefined Layer4Endpoint ECU1_EP".
scenarios.injected_fault: missing or dangling reference (Service Deployment pointing to a non-existent Layer4Endpoint)

scenarios.title: Valid SDConfig with defined timing profile
scenarios.description: Create an SDConfig object that imports a timing profile named 'default_sd' from sd_config.flync.yaml and assigns it to a service.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation succeeds; the SDConfig is accepted and can be used for service discovery.

scenarios.title: SOMEIP datatype size exceeding allowed payload limit
scenarios.description: Define a SOMEIP datatype 'LargePayload' with a fixed length of 2000 bytes, exceeding the typical Ethernet MTU of 1500 bytes and the configured UDP segment size threshold.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation fails with error "Datatype LargePayload size 2000 exceeds maximum allowed payload (1500 bytes) for SOMEIP messages".
scenarios.injected_fault: out-of-range value at or beyond a boundary (max payload)

scenarios.title: Valid SOMEIPServiceProvider with matching interface and endpoint
scenarios.description: Create a SOMEIPServiceProvider that references the previously defined SOMEIPServiceInterface 'EngineControl' and a valid Layer4Endpoint 'ECU1_UDP' (IP 192.168.0.10, port 30490).
scenarios.expected_result: Validation succeeds; the provider is linked to the interface and endpoint.

scenarios.title: SOMEIPServiceConsumer referencing undefined service interface
scenarios.description: Instantiate a SOMEIPServiceConsumer that specifies a service interface name 'NonExistentService' which is not defined in any SOMEIPServiceInterface object.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation fails with error "SOMEIPServiceConsumer references undefined service interface NonExistentService".
scenarios.injected_fault: missing or dangling reference (Service Consumer pointing to a non-existent service interface)

scenarios.title: Valid System Topology Configuration
scenarios.description: A SystemTopology is configured with a single ExternalConnection of type ecu_port_to_ecu_port, connecting two ECUs.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation succeeds, reporting that the SystemTopology is correctly configured with a valid ExternalConnection.

scenarios.title: Invalid ExternalConnection Type
scenarios.description: An ExternalConnection is configured with a type other than ecu_port_to_ecu_port, which is not allowed according to the SystemTopology constraints.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation fails, reporting that the ExternalConnection type is invalid and must be 'ecu_port_to_ecu_port'.
scenarios.injected_fault: Invalid type 'other_type' declared on an ExternalConnection (expected 'ecu_port_to_ecu_port')

scenarios.title: Duplicate ECU Identifier in SystemTopology
scenarios.description: A SystemTopology is configured with two ECUs having the same identifier, which is not allowed according to the SystemTopology constraints.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation fails, reporting that the ECU identifier is duplicated and must be unique.
scenarios.injected_fault: Duplicate identifier 'ecu_id' declared on two ECUs in the SystemTopology

scenarios.title: Missing ECU Reference in ExternalConnection
scenarios.description: An ExternalConnection is configured with a reference to a non-existent ECU, which is not allowed according to the SystemTopology constraints.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation fails, reporting that the ECU reference is missing and must be a valid ECU identifier.
scenarios.injected_fault: Missing ECU reference 'non_existent_ecu' declared on an ExternalConnection

scenarios.title: Valid IPv4 Address in SystemTopology
scenarios.description: A SystemTopology is configured with an IPv4 address that is valid and unique.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation succeeds, reporting that the IPv4 address is valid and correctly configured.

scenarios.title: Duplicate IPv6 Address in SystemTopology
scenarios.description: A SystemTopology is configured with two ECUs having the same IPv6 address, which is not allowed according to the SystemTopology constraints.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation fails, reporting that the IPv6 address is duplicated and must be unique.
scenarios.injected_fault: Duplicate IPv6 address '2001:0db8:85a3:0000:0000:8a2e:0370:7334' declared on two ECUs in the SystemTopology

scenarios.title: Unreachable Multicast Path in SystemTopology
scenarios.description: A SystemTopology is configured with a multicast path that is unreachable due to missing or incorrect VLAN configuration.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation fails, reporting that the multicast path is unreachable and must be correctly configured.
scenarios.injected_fault: Unreachable multicast path due to missing VLAN configuration

scenarios.title: PTPConfig Valid Configuration
scenarios.description: Create a PTPConfig that includes a PTPTimeTransmitterConfig with syncInterval=1s and a PTPTimeReceiverConfig with announceInterval=2s; all required fields are populated with values within spec.
scenarios.expected_result: PTPConfig passes schema validation and can be instantiated without errors.

scenarios.title: PTPPort Invalid Port Number
scenarios.description: Configure a PTPPort with port_number set to 70000, which is outside the allowed 0‑65535 range.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation raises an error stating that 'port_number' must be between 0 and 65535; value 70000 is out of range.
scenarios.injected_fault: out-of-range value at or beyond a boundary (port number)

scenarios.title: CBSShaper Valid Configuration
scenarios.description: Instantiate a CBSShaper with idleCredit=5000 and sendCredit=5000, both within the permitted credit limits, and set a valid maxCredit of 10000.
scenarios.expected_result: CBSShaper passes validation; idleCredit and sendCredit are accepted and the object can be used for traffic shaping.

scenarios.title: ATSInstance Duplicate Identifier
scenarios.description: Add two ATSInstance objects to the model, both using the identifier "ats1".
scenarios.expected_result: Validation fails with a duplicate identifier error: ATSInstance id 'ats1' is already defined.
scenarios.injected_fault: duplicate identifier (ATSInstance ID)

scenarios.title: TrafficClass Valid Configuration
scenarios.description: Create a TrafficClass with priority=3, maxBandwidth=100Mbps, and a non‑zero burstSize, all respecting the link's capacity constraints.
scenarios.expected_result: TrafficClass passes validation; priority is within 0‑7 and bandwidth reservation does not exceed the link capacity.

scenarios.title: HTBInstance Invalid Max Burst
scenarios.description: Configure an HTBInstance with maxBurst set to 2,000,000 bytes, exceeding the allowed maximum of 1,000,000 bytes.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation fails with an error indicating that 'maxBurst' exceeds the maximum allowed size of 1,000,000 bytes (value 2,000,000).
scenarios.injected_fault: out-of-range value at or beyond a boundary (max credit)

scenarios.title: FrameFilter Valid Configuration
scenarios.description: Define a FrameFilter that matches Ethernet type 0x0800 (IPv4) and source MAC address 00:11:22:33:44:55; all required fields are supplied.
scenarios.expected_result: FrameFilter passes validation; filter criteria are syntactically correct and can be applied.

scenarios.title: Stream Invalid Rate
scenarios.description: Create a Stream with rate set to 10 Gbps, which exceeds the maximum allowed stream rate of 1 Gbps for the platform.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation fails with an error stating that the Stream rate (10 Gbps) exceeds the maximum permitted rate of 1 Gbps.
scenarios.injected_fault: out-of-range value at or beyond a boundary (stream rate)

scenarios.title: SingleRateTwoColorMarker Valid Configuration
scenarios.description: Instantiate a SingleRateTwoColorMarker with greenThreshold=80 % and yellowThreshold=95 %, both within the 0‑100 % range, and associate it with a valid TrafficClass.
scenarios.expected_result: SingleRateTwoColorMarker passes validation; thresholds are accepted and the marker can be used for traffic policing.

scenarios.title: DoubleRateThreeColorMarker Missing Reference
scenarios.description: Configure a DoubleRateThreeColorMarker without linking it to a required TrafficClass reference.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation fails with an error indicating that the DoubleRateThreeColorMarker is missing a required reference to a TrafficClass.
scenarios.injected_fault: missing or dangling reference (DoubleRateThreeColorMarker reference)

scenarios.title: App Binding to ECU Controller Participating in CANBus Configuration
scenarios.description: An App containing a ServiceProviderReference is mapped to an ECU controller via AppBindings. This same ECU controller is configured as a participating node on a CANBus defined in the flync_4_bus submodel, which contains inline frames referencing the PDUs that carry the service's signals.
scenarios.expected_result: The configuration validator successfully resolves the mapping, verifying that the App is bound to a controller that is a valid participating node on the CANBus and can transmit the referenced inline frames without any dangling references.

scenarios.title: App ServiceConsumerReference Points to Undefined Service in FLYNCCommunicationConfig
scenarios.description: An App is configured with a ServiceConsumerReference that references a service identifier. However, the corresponding service is not defined within the system-wide FLYNCCommunicationConfig, resulting in a dangling reference across the application and communication submodels.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation fails with a dangling reference error, indicating that the ServiceConsumerReference in the App points to a service identifier that does not exist in the FLYNCCommunicationConfig.
scenarios.injected_fault: ServiceConsumerReference in App references a service identifier that is completely missing from the FLYNCCommunicationConfig

scenarios.title: Valid App Binding of ServiceProvider to ECU Controller
scenarios.description: An App defined in the top-level apps directory containing a ServiceProviderReference is bound to a specific ECU Controller (e.g., hpc_controller1 of an ECU defined in flync_4_ecu) using an AppBindings configuration file located in the controller's directory. The App identifier in AppBindings matches the App's filename on disk.
scenarios.expected_result: The configuration validation succeeds, confirming that the App is successfully bound to the specified ECU Controller and its ServiceProviderReference is correctly resolved.

scenarios.title: AppBindings Deployed to Controller with Dangling Parent ECU Metadata Reference
scenarios.description: An App is bound to an ECU controller using AppBindings. However, the controller's EmbeddedMetadata (defined in controller_metadata.flync.yaml) references a parent ECU identifier that is not declared in any ECUMetadata (ecu_metadata.flync.yaml) file, leaving the application deployment orphaned.
scenarios.expected_result: Configuration validation fails, reporting a dangling reference error because the controller hosting the bound App references an undefined parent ECU identifier.
scenarios.injected_fault: The controller hosting the AppBindings has EmbeddedMetadata pointing to a non-existent parent ECU identifier in ECUMetadata.

scenarios.title: Valid App Binding on Controller with Derived State Management Group Membership
scenarios.description: An App containing a ServiceProviderReference is mapped to an ECU controller using AppBindings. The same ECU controller declares membership in a StateManagementGroup defined in StateManagementConfig. The StateManagementGroup references a GroupTiming profile with a valid cycle_time_ms. This positive scenario verifies that the controller hosting the application is successfully resolved as a member of the network management group, ensuring NM coordination for the application's services.
scenarios.expected_result: The configuration validator successfully processes the AppBindings and derives the controller's membership in the StateManagementGroup, verifying that the hosted App's communication is backed by the active NM group timing profile without errors.

scenarios.title: App ServiceProviderReference Port Blocked by Controller FirewallRule
scenarios.description: An App containing a ServiceProviderReference is bound to an ECU controller via AppBindings. The same ECU controller is configured with a Firewall containing a FirewallRule that matches the destination port of the ServiceProviderReference but has its action set to Drop, rendering the application service unreachable.
scenarios.expected_result: Configuration validation fails, reporting a port conflict where the ServiceProviderReference port is blocked by a Drop action in the FirewallRule of the bound ECU controller.
scenarios.injected_fault: A FirewallRule with action Drop is configured on a controller to block the destination port of a ServiceProviderReference defined within an App that is bound to that controller via AppBindings

scenarios.title: Valid App Binding with Service Provider Reference Mapping to a UINT16 Signal
scenarios.description: An application is defined using the App class, containing a ServiceProviderReference that maps to a transport service. This transport service carries a Signal defined with a SignalDataType of UINT16. The application is successfully bound to an ECU controller via AppBindings.
scenarios.expected_result: The configuration is successfully validated, confirming that the App is correctly bound to the controller via AppBindings and its associated ServiceProviderReference successfully maps to the transport service carrying the valid UINT16 Signal.

scenarios.title: App ServiceConsumerReference Points to Undefined SOME/IP Service Interface
scenarios.description: An App defined in the apps directory contains a ServiceConsumerReference that references a SOME/IP service interface. However, this service interface is not declared within the SOME/IP configuration under communication/someip/ (SOMEIPConfig), resulting in an unresolved dependency when the App is bound via AppBindings.
scenarios.expected_result: Configuration validation fails with a dangling reference error, reporting that the service interface referenced by the App's ServiceConsumerReference does not exist in the SOME/IP configuration.
scenarios.injected_fault: ServiceConsumerReference in App references a service interface identifier that is missing from the SOME/IP configuration

scenarios.title: Valid Service Communication Path via AppBindings and SystemTopology ExternalConnection
scenarios.description: An App 'App_Provider' declaring a ServiceProviderReference is bound to an ECU Controller via AppBindings, and another App 'App_Consumer' declaring a ServiceConsumerReference is bound to a different ECU Controller via AppBindings. The SystemTopology defines a valid ExternalConnection of type 'ecu_port_to_ecu_port' between the ports of the respective ECUs hosting these controllers, enabling valid cross-ECU service communication.
scenarios.expected_result: The configuration validates successfully, confirming that the service consumer App and service provider App are bound to controllers on ECUs that are physically connected via a declared ExternalConnection in the SystemTopology.

scenarios.title: TSN Stream Ingress Policing Configured on Controller Lacking App Binding
scenarios.description: An App defines a ServiceProviderReference for a service. A TSN Stream is configured with an ATSInstance and SingleRateTwoColorMarker on a specific controller's network interface to police this service's traffic. However, the AppBindings configuration binds this App to a different controller, causing a mismatch where the TSN Stream is configured on a controller that does not host the application.
scenarios.expected_result: Configuration validation fails, reporting a deployment mismatch between the App's controller binding in AppBindings and the controller interface hosting the TSN Stream.
scenarios.injected_fault: The App containing the ServiceProviderReference is bound via AppBindings to a controller that does not match the controller interface where the TSN Stream and ATSInstance are configured.

scenarios.title: Valid CANBus Inline Frame PDU Reference Resolution within FLYNCChannelConfig
scenarios.description: A system configuration defines a FLYNCCommunicationConfig containing a FLYNCChannelConfig. Under the communication/channels/can/ directory, a CANBus configuration file is defined with an inline frame that references a PDU via the pdu_ref field. This referenced PDU is successfully defined in a separate file under communication/channels/pdus/.
scenarios.expected_result: The configuration validation succeeds, confirming that the FLYNCChannelConfig correctly resolves the pdu_ref in the CANBus inline frame to the corresponding PDU definition under the pdus directory.

scenarios.title: CANBus Participating Node References ECU with Missing ECUPort
scenarios.description: A CANBus configuration defined under communication/channels/can/ references a participating ECU node. However, the ECU's configuration defined via flync_4_ecu in ports.flync.yaml does not contain any ECUPort configured to connect to this CANBus.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation fails with a reference error indicating that the ECU listed as a participating node in the CANBus configuration lacks a corresponding ECUPort in ports.flync.yaml.
scenarios.injected_fault: CANBus participating node references an ECU that has no matching ECUPort defined in ports.flync.yaml

scenarios.title: CANBus Participating Nodes Correctly Reference Defined ECUMetadata Identifiers
scenarios.description: A CANBus configuration is defined in communication/channels/can/powertrain_can.flync.yaml using the flync.model.flync_4_bus.CANBus class, specifying 'high_performance_compute' as a participating node. This node identifier matches the unique ECU identifier declared in ecu_metadata.flync.yaml using the flync.model.flync_4_metadata.ECUMetadata class.
scenarios.expected_result: The configuration validation succeeds, verifying that the participating node on the CANBus correctly resolves to the defined ECUMetadata identifier with no dangling references.

scenarios.title: CANBus Declares StateManagementGroup Membership Without Mapping the Group NM PDU
scenarios.description: A CANBus configuration declares membership in a StateManagementGroup defined in groups.flync.yaml. The StateManagementGroup references an NM PDU with pdu_usage set to network_management. However, the inline Frames defined within the CANBus YAML configuration do not contain any Frame referencing this NM PDU via pdu_ref, preventing the bus from transmitting the required network management signals.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation fails, reporting that the CANBus is declared as a member of the StateManagementGroup but does not route the group's designated NM PDU.
scenarios.injected_fault: CANBus declares membership in a StateManagementGroup but does not define an inline Frame referencing the group's NM PDU via pdu_ref

scenarios.title: Valid FirewallRule Reference to CANBus Participating Node
scenarios.description: A CANBus configuration is defined under flync_4_bus containing a list of participating nodes, including a gateway node named 'SecGW'. Concurrently, a Firewall configuration is defined under flync_4_security containing a FirewallRule whose source or destination ECU identifier correctly references the 'SecGW' node. The validator cross-references the security rules with the physical bus topology.
scenarios.expected_result: The configuration validation succeeds with zero errors, confirming that the FirewallRule's ECU identifier successfully resolves to the active participating node defined within the CANBus configuration.

scenarios.title: SignalInstance in PDU Exceeds CANBus Frame Payload Limit
scenarios.description: A classic CANBus configuration defines an inline Frame referencing a PDU via pdu_ref. This PDU contains a SignalInstance wrapping a Signal defined with a SignalDataType of BYTEARRAY configured with a size of 16 bytes, which exceeds the 8-byte (64-bit) maximum payload limit of a Classic CAN frame.
scenarios.expected_result: Configuration validation fails, reporting that the total bit-width of the SignalInstance in the PDU referenced by the CANBus Frame exceeds the 8-byte limit for Classic CAN.
scenarios.injected_fault: A 16-byte BYTEARRAY Signal is mapped via a SignalInstance to a PDU carried by a classic CANBus Frame, exceeding the 8-byte payload limit

scenarios.title: SOMEIPServiceDeployment Binding to Ethernet Bus Node Endpoint
scenarios.description: An Ethernet physical communication bus is configured under 'communication/channels/' (defined by flync_4_bus) containing a participating node with a declared IP address. A SOME/IP service interface is configured in 'communication/someip/' using SOMEIPConfig and SDConfig (defined by flync_4_someip), and its deployment successfully binds to the Layer4Endpoint (IP and port) of that participating node on the Ethernet bus.
scenarios.expected_result: The configuration validator successfully parses both submodels, verifying that the SOME/IP service deployment correctly resolves its target Layer4Endpoint to the valid IP address of the participating node defined on the Ethernet communication bus.

scenarios.title: CANBus Participating Nodes Lack Valid ecu_port_to_ecu_port Connection in SystemTopology
scenarios.description: A CANBus configuration defines ECU_A and ECU_B as participating nodes to exchange inline frames. To establish the physical link, SystemTopology defines an ExternalConnection between these ECUs, but the connection's 'type' field is set to 'ecu_to_bus' instead of the strictly required 'ecu_port_to_ecu_port'.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation fails with a configuration error indicating that the ExternalConnection between the CANBus participating nodes is not of type 'ecu_port_to_ecu_port'.
scenarios.injected_fault: ExternalConnection type in SystemTopology configured as 'ecu_to_bus' instead of 'ecu_port_to_ecu_port' for ECUs participating in the CANBus

scenarios.title: Valid TSN FrameFilter Reference to Inline Frame in CANBus Configuration
scenarios.description: A CANBus configuration in flync_4_bus defines an inline frame referencing a PDU. In flync_4_tsn, a FrameFilter is configured within a Stream to perform ingress policing using a SingleRateTwoColorMarker. The FrameFilter correctly references the inline frame defined in the CANBus configuration, establishing a valid cross-module association for traffic shaping.
scenarios.expected_result: The configuration validation passes successfully, confirming that the FrameFilter in flync_4_tsn correctly resolves the reference to the inline frame defined within the CANBus configuration of flync_4_bus.

scenarios.title: ECU TCPOption References Undefined TCP Profile in FLYNCCommunicationConfig
scenarios.description: An ECU configured via flync.model.flync_4_ecu.ecu.ECU contains a socket configuration using flync.model.flync_4_ecu.sockets.TCPOption which attempts to import a TCP profile. However, the referenced TCP profile identifier is completely missing from the system-wide TCP profiles defined in flync.model.flync_4_communication.FLYNCCommunicationConfig.
scenarios.expected_result: Configuration validation fails, reporting a dangling reference error because the TCP profile imported by the ECU's TCPOption cannot be resolved in the FLYNCCommunicationConfig.
scenarios.injected_fault: ECU socket TCPOption references a TCP profile name that does not exist in the FLYNCCommunicationConfig TCP profiles list

scenarios.title: Valid FLYNCCommunicationConfig Integration with Compliant SystemMetadata and ECUMetadata
scenarios.description: A complete system configuration is defined where the system-wide communication parameters are specified in a FLYNCCommunicationConfig (including channel definitions under FLYNCChannelConfig). Concurrently, the mandatory system context is defined in SystemMetadata with a valid semantic version of '2.0.0', and the associated ECUs are defined with unique ECUMetadata identifiers. Both submodels are loaded together to establish a fully compatible and traceable network configuration.
scenarios.expected_result: The FLYNC configuration parser successfully validates both the FLYNCCommunicationConfig and the SystemMetadata/ECUMetadata, verifying that the communication channels are correctly aligned with a valid system context and unique ECU identifiers without any duplicate-identifier or version-parsing errors.

scenarios.title: StateManagementGroup References PDU Without Network Management Usage in FLYNCChannelConfig
scenarios.description: A StateManagementGroup is defined within StateManagementConfig (flync_4_nm) and references a PDU identifier. However, the corresponding PDU defined within FLYNCChannelConfig (flync_4_communication) does not have its usage configured as network_management (pdu_usage: network_management), instead being defined as an ordinary application PDU.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation fails with a configuration error indicating that the PDU referenced by the StateManagementGroup must have its usage set to 'network_management' in the FLYNCChannelConfig.
scenarios.injected_fault: StateManagementGroup references a PDU from FLYNCChannelConfig that lacks the required 'pdu_usage: network_management' configuration.

scenarios.title: Valid Firewall Rule Destination Port Matching TCPOption Socket Configuration
scenarios.description: A system-wide configuration defines a TCP profile using TCPOption under FLYNCCommunicationConfig with a specific local port. In the flync_4_security submodel, a Firewall is configured with a FirewallRule whose destination port matches this TCPOption port, allowing traffic to pass through the firewall to the socket.
scenarios.expected_result: The configuration validator successfully verifies the FirewallRule, confirming that the destination port is within the valid 0-65535 range and correctly aligns with the active socket port defined in the FLYNCCommunicationConfig.

scenarios.title: SignalInstance Placement in FLYNCChannelConfig Classic CAN PDU Exceeds 8-Byte Payload Limit
scenarios.description: A FLYNCChannelConfig defines a Classic CAN bus channel with a PDU. A SignalInstance from flync_4_signal wraps a Signal of SignalDataType UINT64 (natural_bit_width of 64 bits) and is placed in this PDU at a bit offset of 16. This forces the total PDU size to 80 bits (10 bytes), which exceeds the Classic CAN maximum payload limit of 8 bytes.
scenarios.expected_result: The configuration validator fails, reporting that the PDU size (80 bits) exceeds the 8-byte (64-bit) maximum payload limit for Classic CAN defined in the FLYNCChannelConfig.
scenarios.injected_fault: A 64-bit SignalInstance is placed at bit offset 16 within a Classic CAN PDU defined in FLYNCChannelConfig, exceeding the 8-byte payload limit.

scenarios.title: SOME/IP Service Deployment with SDTimings and TCPOption Integration
scenarios.description: A valid configuration where a SOME/IP service defined in SOMEIPConfig (from flync_4_someip) is deployed on an ECU socket. The deployment references an SDTimings profile defined within SDConfig (from flync_4_someip) for its Service Discovery behavior, and the underlying TCP socket imports a TCPOption profile defined within the FLYNCCommunicationConfig (from flync_4_communication) under communication/channels/ via FLYNCChannelConfig. All references resolve correctly.
scenarios.expected_result: The configuration generator successfully validates the model, verifying that the SOMEIPConfig service deployment correctly binds the SDTimings parameters and the TCPOption socket parameters without any unresolved references or validation errors.

scenarios.title: SystemTopology ExternalConnection Port Protocol Mismatch with FLYNCChannelConfig Bus Definition
scenarios.description: A SystemTopology defines an ExternalConnection of type 'ecu_port_to_ecu_port' connecting Port_A of ECU_1 and Port_B of ECU_2. However, in the FLYNCChannelConfig, Port_A is configured as part of a CAN bus channel, while Port_B is configured as part of an Ethernet channel, creating an incompatible physical connection between the two ECUs.
scenarios.expected_result: Configuration validation fails with a protocol mismatch error, indicating that the connected ports in the SystemTopology ExternalConnection must share compatible bus technologies in FLYNCChannelConfig.
scenarios.injected_fault: An ExternalConnection in SystemTopology connects a CAN-configured port to an Ethernet-configured port as defined in FLYNCChannelConfig.

scenarios.title: TSN Stream Ingress Policing for Ethernet Channel Frames
scenarios.description: A valid configuration where an Ethernet communication channel and its associated frame/PDU definitions are configured under FLYNCChannelConfig (from flync_4_communication). To manage bandwidth, a TSN Stream (from flync_4_tsn) is configured to filter this channel's traffic using an ATSInstance and a SingleRateTwoColorMarker for ingress policing.
scenarios.expected_result: The configuration validator successfully validates the network model, confirming that the Stream and ATSInstance from flync_4_tsn are correctly mapped to the Ethernet channel and frame definitions defined in FLYNCChannelConfig from flync_4_communication without any validation errors.

scenarios.title: EmbeddedMetadata Parent ECU Identifier Mismatch with ECUMetadata Identifier
scenarios.description: An ECU is configured using the ECU class from flync_4_ecu, and its system-level identification is defined in ECUMetadata (ecu_metadata.flync.yaml) with the identifier 'HPC_ECU_01'. A Controller is configured on this ECU, and its associated EmbeddedMetadata (controller_metadata.flync.yaml) references a parent ECU identifier 'HPC_ECU_99' which does not match the identifier declared in ECUMetadata.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation fails with a dangling reference error, indicating that the parent ECU identifier 'HPC_ECU_99' in the controller's EmbeddedMetadata does not resolve to any declared ECUMetadata identifier in the system configuration.
scenarios.injected_fault: EmbeddedMetadata parent ECU identifier references a non-existent ECU identifier ('HPC_ECU_99') instead of the declared ECUMetadata identifier ('HPC_ECU_01')

scenarios.title: Valid ECU State Management Group Membership and Timing Profile Association
scenarios.description: An ECU is configured with a declared membership in a StateManagementGroup. The StateManagementGroup is defined in the StateManagementConfig with a valid GroupTiming profile (e.g., cycle_time_ms: 500) and an NM PDU reference. The validation engine resolves the membership entity-side from the ECU to derive the effective member set of the StateManagementGroup.
scenarios.expected_result: Configuration validation succeeds, successfully deriving the ECU as a member of the StateManagementGroup and verifying that the timing profile parameters are correctly applied to the derived member.

scenarios.title: FirewallRule References Non-Existent ECUPort Identifier
scenarios.description: A FirewallRule configured within a Firewall in the flync_4_security submodel attempts to reference an ECUPort from the flync_4_ecu submodel as its target interface, but the specified ECUPort identifier does not exist in the ECU configuration.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation fails with a dangling reference error, explicitly stating that the ECUPort identifier referenced by the FirewallRule is undefined in the ECU Ports Config.
scenarios.injected_fault: FirewallRule references a non-existent ECUPort identifier as its network interface

scenarios.title: ECUPort Network Mapping of SignalInstance with Valid SignalDataType
scenarios.description: An ECU of class flync.model.flync_4_ecu.ecu.ECU is configured with an ECUPort from flync.model.flync_4_ecu.port.ECUPort. A Signal of class flync.model.flync_4_signal.Signal is defined with a SignalDataType of UINT16 (which has a natural_bit_width of 16 bits). This Signal is wrapped in a SignalInstance with a valid bit offset and byte order, placing it inside a PDU that is mapped to be transmitted via the ECUPort.
scenarios.expected_result: The configuration validator successfully parses both submodels, confirming that the 16-bit SignalInstance fits within the PDU payload and is correctly mapped to the ECUPort without any validation errors.

scenarios.title: SOME/IP Service Deployment to ECU Controller Missing Mandatory ECUPort Configuration
scenarios.description: A SOME/IP service configured under SOMEIPConfig is deployed to a controller of an ECU. However, the target ECU has no ECUPort configured in its mandatory ports.flync.yaml file, violating the rule that all ECUs must define at least one port to enable physical network communication.
scenarios.expected_result: Configuration validation fails, reporting that the target ECU for the SOME/IP service deployment is invalid because it lacks the mandatory ECUPort configuration.
scenarios.injected_fault: SOME/IP service deployment targeted to an ECU controller where the parent ECU has zero ECUPort definitions in ports.flync.yaml

scenarios.title: Valid ExternalConnection Mapping Between Defined ECUPorts in SystemTopology
scenarios.description: A system configuration defines two instances of flync.model.flync_4_ecu.ecu.ECU, each configuring at least one flync.model.flync_4_ecu.port.ECUPort in its ports configuration. In the flync.model.flync_4_topology.SystemTopology, a flync.model.flync_4_topology.ExternalConnection is defined with type 'ecu_port_to_ecu_port' to establish a physical link between these two ports.
scenarios.expected_result: The network configuration model successfully validates the system topology, resolving the ExternalConnection references to the declared ECUPort instances on both ECUs without any validation errors.

scenarios.title: PTPPort References Undefined ECUPort in ECU Configuration
scenarios.description: A PTPPort within PTPConfig (from flync_4_tsn) is configured for gPTP time synchronization, but its referenced port identifier does not match any ECUPort defined in the ECU ports configuration (from flync_4_ecu).
scenarios.expected_result: Validation fails with a dangling reference error, stating that the PTPPort references an undefined ECUPort 'eth_tsn_0'.
scenarios.injected_fault: PTPPort references an ECUPort identifier 'eth_tsn_0' which is missing from the ECUPort configurations defined in ports.flync.yaml

scenarios.title: ECUMetadata Declares Valid Membership in StateManagementGroup for Effective Member Set Derivation
scenarios.description: A system configuration defines an ECU with a unique identifier in ECUMetadata. In StateManagementConfig, a StateManagementGroup is defined referencing a GroupTiming profile. The ECU declares its membership in the StateManagementGroup on the entity side. During validation, the compiler successfully resolves the ECU's metadata identifier and derives the effective member set of the StateManagementGroup to include this ECU.
scenarios.expected_result: The configuration validates successfully, and the derived member set of the StateManagementGroup is resolved to contain the ECU identifier defined in ECUMetadata without any dangling references or validation errors.

scenarios.title: Valid System and ECU Metadata Configuration with Standard Signal and SignalInstance Definitions
scenarios.description: A FLYNC network configuration is defined with a mandatory SystemMetadata file using a valid Semantic Versioning 2.0.0 version string ('1.0.0') and an ECUMetadata file defining a unique ECU identifier 'ECU_01'. In the same configuration, a Signal is defined with a SignalDataType of 'UINT16' (exposing a natural_bit_width of 16), which is successfully wrapped in a SignalInstance with valid bit offset and byte order. Both submodels are loaded together to form a complete, valid configuration.
scenarios.expected_result: The configuration validation tool successfully parses both submodels, verifying that the SystemMetadata semantic version is valid, the ECU identifier is unique, and the Signal's SignalDataType is correctly resolved to 'UINT16' with no validation errors.

scenarios.title: SOME/IP Service Deployment References Socket on Undefined ECU Metadata
scenarios.description: A SOME/IP service deployment defined under flync_4_someip (within SOMEIPConfig) binds a service interface to a Layer4Endpoint on a specific ECU socket. However, the target ECU identifier specified for this deployment does not exist in the system configuration because no corresponding ECUMetadata block is defined in flync_4_metadata.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation fails with a dangling reference error, indicating that the SOME/IP service deployment targets an ECU identifier not declared in any ECUMetadata configuration.
scenarios.injected_fault: SOME/IP service deployment references a Layer4Endpoint on an ECU identifier that is missing from the ECUMetadata configuration

scenarios.title: Valid External Connection Mapping Between Declared ECUMetadata Identifiers in SystemTopology
scenarios.description: A system configuration defines two distinct ECUs using ECUMetadata with unique identifiers (e.g., 'HPC_ECU' and 'Zone_ECU'). A SystemTopology is configured with an ExternalConnection of type 'ecu_port_to_ecu_port' that references the ports of these two declared ECUs. Both submodels are fully consistent, with no dangling references.
scenarios.expected_result: The configuration passes validation successfully, verifying that the ECU identifiers referenced in the SystemTopology's ExternalConnection map to existing ECUMetadata declarations and the connection type is correctly set to 'ecu_port_to_ecu_port'.

scenarios.title: PTPConfig Deployment on Controller with Dangling Parent ECU Reference in EmbeddedMetadata
scenarios.description: A PTPConfig containing a PTPPort is configured for a network controller. The controller's EmbeddedMetadata references a parent ECU identifier that is not declared in any ECUMetadata file, resulting in an unresolved hardware association for the time synchronization configuration.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation fails with a reference error, indicating that the PTPConfig cannot be resolved because the controller's EmbeddedMetadata contains a dangling reference to a non-existent parent ECU identifier.
scenarios.injected_fault: EmbeddedMetadata for a controller hosting a PTPConfig references a non-existent parent ECU identifier.

scenarios.title: StateManagementGroup NM PDU Traffic Permitted by Controller FirewallRule
scenarios.description: A StateManagementGroup is configured with an NM PDU where pdu_usage is set to network_management. The ECU controller transmitting this NM PDU is secured with a Firewall containing a FirewallRule. The FirewallRule is configured to allow UDP traffic matching the specific destination port and IP address of the network management PDU.
scenarios.expected_result: The configuration validation succeeds, verifying that the network management PDU's destination port and IP address are correctly permitted by the FirewallRule within the Firewall configuration, allowing NM state management communication to proceed.

scenarios.title: StateManagementGroup NM PDU Contains SignalInstance with Invalid SignalDataType
scenarios.description: A StateManagementGroup is configured to reference an ordinary NM PDU (with pdu_usage set to network_management). However, this PDU contains a SignalInstance wrapping a Signal defined with a SignalDataType of FLOAT32, which is incompatible with network management PDUs that require integer-based control or node identifiers.
scenarios.expected_result: Configuration validation fails, reporting that the StateManagementGroup's referenced NM PDU contains a SignalInstance with an invalid SignalDataType (FLOAT32) for network management usage.
scenarios.injected_fault: An NM PDU referenced by a StateManagementGroup contains a SignalInstance with a FLOAT32 SignalDataType

scenarios.title: Aligned StateManagementGroup SleepTiming and SOME/IP SDTimings for Active Service Discovery
scenarios.description: A valid network configuration defines a StateManagementGroup in StateManagementConfig (from flync_4_nm) referencing a GroupTiming with a cycle_time_ms of 500ms and a SleepTiming profile. Concurrently, a SOMEIPConfig (from flync_4_someip) defines an SDConfig with SDTimings for service discovery. The SOME/IP-SD cyclic offer transmission interval within SDTimings is configured to be shorter than the network sleep timeout defined in SleepTiming, ensuring that SOME/IP-SD messages are successfully transmitted before the state management group transitions the bus to sleep.
scenarios.expected_result: The configuration validation succeeds, verifying that the SOME/IP-SD cyclic transmission interval in SDTimings is compatible with the SleepTiming and GroupTiming cycle_time_ms, allowing both the flync_4_nm and flync_4_someip submodels to be successfully validated and generated.

scenarios.title: StateManagementGroup Member ECU Lacks ExternalConnection in SystemTopology
scenarios.description: An ECU is configured with a membership in a StateManagementGroup (defined within StateManagementConfig), but the SystemTopology of the FLYNCTopology contains no ExternalConnection of type 'ecu_port_to_ecu_port' for this ECU, leaving the derived group member topologically isolated and unable to exchange the network management PDU.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation fails with a cross-module error indicating that the derived member ECU of the StateManagementGroup lacks a valid ExternalConnection in the SystemTopology configuration.
scenarios.injected_fault: ECU declared as a StateManagementGroup member has no ExternalConnection defined in SystemTopology

scenarios.title: StateManagementGroup Timing Alignment with TSN Stream Ingress Policing
scenarios.description: A StateManagementGroup is configured with a GroupTiming profile specifying a cycle_time_ms of 500 for its network management PDU (pdu_usage: network_management). The network management PDU is mapped to a TSN Stream configured with a SingleRateTwoColorMarker for ingress policing. The SingleRateTwoColorMarker is configured with a committed information rate that is mathematically sufficient to allow the periodic NM PDU transmissions without triggering policing drops.
scenarios.expected_result: The system configuration successfully passes validation, confirming that the TSN Stream's SingleRateTwoColorMarker bandwidth allocation is compatible with the periodic transmission rate defined by the StateManagementGroup's GroupTiming cycle_time_ms.

scenarios.title: FirewallRule Value Filtering on BYTEARRAY SignalDataType
scenarios.description: A FirewallRule in flync_4_security is configured to filter network traffic by performing a scalar value comparison against a specific Signal defined in flync_4_signal. However, the referenced Signal is configured with a SignalDataType of BYTEARRAY, which is incompatible with scalar comparison operators.
scenarios.expected_result: Configuration validation fails, reporting that the FirewallRule cannot apply scalar comparison operators to a Signal of non-scalar SignalDataType BYTEARRAY.
scenarios.injected_fault: FirewallRule configured with a scalar comparison against a Signal defined with a BYTEARRAY SignalDataType

scenarios.title: Firewall Rule Configuration Permitting SOME/IP Service and Service Discovery Traffic
scenarios.description: A valid system configuration where a SOME/IP service is deployed via SOMEIPConfig on a specific UDP port, and Service Discovery is configured via SDConfig on the standard UDP port 30490. To allow this communication, the ECU's Firewall is configured with FirewallRule instances that explicitly match and allow traffic targeting the SOME/IP service port and the SOME/IP-SD multicast port.
scenarios.expected_result: The configuration validator successfully verifies that the FirewallRule port and address parameters correctly encompass the UDP ports defined in SOMEIPConfig and SDConfig, ensuring SOME/IP and Service Discovery traffic is not blocked.

scenarios.title: FirewallRule References ECU Identifier Missing from SystemTopology ExternalConnection
scenarios.description: A Firewall configuration defines a FirewallRule targeting a specific ECU identifier for traffic filtering. However, in the SystemTopology, the ExternalConnection list (which must be of type 'ecu_port_to_ecu_port') does not define or reference this ECU identifier, resulting in a dangling reference.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation fails with a dangling reference error, indicating that the ECU identifier specified in the FirewallRule does not exist in the SystemTopology configuration.
scenarios.injected_fault: FirewallRule references an ECU identifier that is not declared in any ExternalConnection of the SystemTopology

scenarios.title: Coexistence of MACsec Link Security and gPTP Time Synchronization on a TSN Port
scenarios.description: A TSN Ethernet port is configured to secure link-layer traffic using MACsec and simultaneously perform gPTP time synchronization. The security configuration defines a MACsecConfig utilizing IntegrityWithConfidentiality. The TSN configuration defines a PTPConfig containing a PTPPort associated with a PTPTimeTransmitterConfig on the same interface. This represents a valid secure TSN deployment where gPTP frames are protected by MACsec.
scenarios.expected_result: The configuration validator successfully validates the model, confirming that the network interface is correctly bound to both the MACsecConfig (with IntegrityWithConfidentiality) and the PTPConfig (with PTPPort and PTPTimeTransmitterConfig) without validation errors.

scenarios.title: Signal BYTEARRAY Payload Exceeds SOMEIPConfig UDP Threshold Without SOME/IP TP
scenarios.description: A Signal defined with SignalDataType BYTEARRAY of size 2048 bytes is mapped via a SignalInstance to a PDU carried by a SOME/IP Service Interface event. However, the associated SOMEIPConfig defines a UDP segment size threshold of 1416 bytes and does not have SOME/IP TP (Transport Protocol) enabled for this service.
scenarios.expected_result: Validation fails with an error stating that the payload size of the Signal exceeds the configured SOMEIPConfig UDP segment size threshold and SOME/IP TP is not enabled to handle segmentation.
scenarios.injected_fault: A 2048-byte BYTEARRAY Signal is mapped to a SOME/IP Service Interface event whose SOMEIPConfig UDP segment threshold is 1416 bytes without SOME/IP TP enabled

scenarios.title: Valid Signal Mapping Over Topology External Connection
scenarios.description: A Signal is defined with a SignalDataType of UINT16 (which has a natural_bit_width of 16) and is instantiated via a SignalInstance. The communication path for this signal maps perfectly to a physical link defined in SystemTopology using an ExternalConnection with type set to 'ecu_port_to_ecu_port', connecting the source and destination ECU ports.
scenarios.expected_result: The configuration validator successfully parses the model, confirming that the SignalInstance's logical path is fully supported by the physical ExternalConnection of type 'ecu_port_to_ecu_port' defined in the SystemTopology.

scenarios.title: SignalInstance Width Exceeds TSN FrameFilter Maximum Frame Length
scenarios.description: A Signal is defined with a SignalDataType of BYTEARRAY requiring 128 bytes of payload and is instantiated via a SignalInstance inside a Frame. This Frame is routed through a TSN network path where a FrameFilter in flync_4_tsn is configured to police the corresponding Stream with a maximum frame length limit of 64 bytes.
scenarios.expected_result: Configuration validation fails, reporting that the minimum frame size required by the SignalInstance (128 bytes) exceeds the maximum frame length of the matching TSN FrameFilter (64 bytes).
scenarios.injected_fault: A 128-byte BYTEARRAY SignalInstance is mapped to a Frame governed by a TSN FrameFilter configured with a maximum frame length of 64 bytes

scenarios.title: Valid SOME/IP Service Discovery Deployment over Topology External Connection
scenarios.description: A valid network configuration where the FLYNCTopology defines a SystemTopology containing an ExternalConnection of type 'ecu_port_to_ecu_port' between two ECUs. Concurrently, the SOMEIPConfig (placed in the communication/someip/ directory) defines an SDConfig with SDTimings for SOME/IP Service Discovery. The SOME/IP service is deployed on an ECU socket on one of the connected ECUs, allowing service discovery messages to be routed across the defined physical connection.
scenarios.expected_result: The configuration validation succeeds. The generator successfully maps the SOME/IP-SD timing profiles from SDTimings to the endpoints of the ECUs linked by the ExternalConnection of type 'ecu_port_to_ecu_port' in the SystemTopology.

scenarios.title: SOME/IP-SD Timing Profile Message Rate Exceeds TSN Ingress Stream Policer Committed Information Rate
scenarios.description: A SOME/IP Service Discovery configuration (SDConfig) defines a highly frequent message interval in SDTimings for service discovery. However, the TSN ingress policing configuration for this traffic, defined via a TSN Stream with a FrameFilter matching the SOME/IP-SD multicast address, uses a SingleRateTwoColorMarker whose committed information rate (CIR) is configured too low to sustain the periodic SD messages, leading to dropped SD packets.
scenarios.expected_result: Configuration validation fails with an error indicating that the TSN Stream's SingleRateTwoColorMarker bandwidth is insufficient for the configured SOME/IP-SD SDTimings rate.
scenarios.injected_fault: SOME/IP-SD message transmission rate defined in SDTimings exceeds the committed information rate (CIR) of the SingleRateTwoColorMarker assigned to the TSN Stream filtering the SD traffic.

scenarios.title: Valid gPTP Time Synchronization Link Across Topology External Connection
scenarios.description: A system topology is defined in SystemTopology containing an ExternalConnection of type ecu_port_to_ecu_port connecting Port A of ECU_1 to Port B of ECU_2. In the TSN configuration (PTPConfig), Port A is configured as a PTPPort referencing a PTPTimeTransmitterConfig, and Port B is configured as a PTPPort referencing a PTPTimeReceiverConfig. Both ports use matching PTPPdelayConfig parameters to measure link delay across this connection.
scenarios.expected_result: The validation engine successfully parses both submodels, verifying that the PTPPort configurations for Port A and Port B correctly map to the endpoints of the ExternalConnection defined in SystemTopology, and confirms that a valid time synchronization path is established between the transmitter and receiver.
